A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 22-page versions of the same ToMA paper, including Appendices A–H. Extracted text and rendered pages 2–22 are identical; the differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-quality and latency experiments on SDXL-base and Flux.1-dev in Tables 1–3, plus ablations and memory measurements in Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v3 retains the original SDXL-base and Flux.1-dev experiments, ablations, qualitative outputs, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The facility-location selection, attention-based merging, transpose-based unmerging, locality and reuse procedures, and DiT adaptations are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A, B, and E.

E1.justification: Both versions use GEMRec and ImageNet-1K prompts for SDXL-base and Flux.1-dev image generation. No datasets, tasks, or qualitative test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains ToMe/ToMeSD, ToFu, ToDo, and the SDXL baseline. TLB and appendix comparator sets are also unchanged; Flux remains evaluated without those competing token-reduction methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.1, table captions, and appendices retain the same sample sizes, metrics, hardware, merge settings, and testing procedures, including 1024×1024 generation with 50 SDXL steps or 35 Flux steps.

E4.justification: Appendix F retains the same destination-selection, tile-granularity, kernel-latency, unmerge, and recomputation-schedule ablations. Qualitative examples, locality analyses, and memory profiling are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 retains three seeds per ablation prompt and median inference timings over 100 runs; Table 6 retains medians over 1,000 runs. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedures are added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and the qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports ToMA at 5.04 seconds/image and FID 28.9 for a 0.50 merge ratio in both versions.

T1.justification: The submodular definitions and greedy guarantee, merge/unmerge mathematics, facility-location derivation, and computational-complexity analysis are identical in both versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and efficiency-quality claims, including the abstract's 24% SDXL and 23% Flux latency reductions.

C2.justification: The speed-quality interpretations, locality and reuse explanations, DiT positional-embedding restrictions, and discussion of future kernel optimization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds 'Code available at github.com/WenboLuu/ToMA' to the abstract; v1 contains no ToMA repository address. This adds code-access information without changing documented implementation details or settings.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the paper's positioning relative to prior token-reduction methods are unchanged. No cited research works are added or removed.

P1.justification: A short code-availability sentence is appended to the abstract, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added hyperlink causes limited reflow and vertical repositioning of the abstract on page 1. All figures, tables, and layouts on pages 2–22 remain identical.

improvement.justification: The new implementation link provides a small, concrete improvement in code discoverability and reproducibility guidance. Scientific content and evidence, including all appendices, are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked repository's completeness or usability.
